decisions.quote:
Stage 1 is a replication study of the Maritz et al (2015) study, with extension of nascent support mechanisms. As such, we commence with a five-year longitudinal comparison of EEPs in Australian HEIs (2014 and 2019).
The replication component of this article consists of a quantitative measurement of EEPs, consisting of full programs, programs with majors and/or minors, and subjects either about or related to entrepreneurship. Findings reflect a somewhat subdued outcome between 2014 and 2019, with EEPs virtually identical (50 versus 53) and subjects (584 versus 463). The latter indicates a decline of approximately 20% over the five-year period.
decisions.location: Findings and Discussion, Stage 1 Entrepreneurship Education Offerings (Quantitative), lines 33-34
decisions.reason: Stage 1 explicitly replicates the quantitative survey of Australian HEI entrepreneurship education offerings from Maritz et al. (2015) and compares the 2019 results directly against the 2014/2015 baseline. Under Codebook Rule 2, where no single categorical confirmation/refutation sentence is phrased as an overall verdict, the outcome is coded from the authors' explicit comparisons to the original study: some findings held across the replication (total EEPs remained virtually identical at 50 vs 53, and the sparse, inconsistent distribution across the 40 HEIs persisted), whereas other core measures diverged substantially (total entrepreneurship subjects declined by ~20% from 584 to 463, and individual university rankings exhibited high fluidity in contrast to aggregate EEP stasis). Because the authors' explicit comparisons partly agree with and partly diverge from the 2015 baseline, the outcome is 'mixed' rather than 'cannot_be_determined'.
